PullRequest.Title: Keep context views and menus clear of Window Controls Overlay buttons
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #165454

When the Window Controls Overlay (WCO) is shown, context views, context menus and submenus could be placed on top of the native window control buttons, where they could not be seen or clicked.

This change adds a pure helper, `avoidWindowControlsOverlay` (`src/vs/base/browser/ui/contextview/windowControlsOverlay.ts`). Both `ContextView` and `Menu` submenus use it:
- It reads the overlay geometry from the target window (`navigator.windowControlsOverlay`), so auxiliary windows are handled correctly.
- If a widget would overlap the button area at the top, it moves below the title bar band. If it overlaps exactly one side strip and does not fit below, it shifts horizontally instead.
- If neither placement works, the widget is clamped so it stays inside the viewport instead of being pushed off-screen.

## How to test

```
npm run transpile-client
npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/contextview/windowControlsOverlay.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/contextview/contextview.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/menu/menu.test.ts (plus the menubar, contextMenuHandler and contextViewService suites) --browser chromium
```
Result: **120 passing** (six suites). The tests stub `navigator.windowControlsOverlay` per window and restore it after each test.

To check manually on Windows with a custom title bar: open a context menu or submenu near the top-right window controls. The menu should stay clear of the minimize, maximize and close buttons.

Note: the visual verification stubbed the overlay geometry on macOS. Native Windows WCO was not checked on a real device.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show or relayout a context view, including menus, hovers, and action widgets near the title bar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ContextView.show/layout synchronously measures the anchor and view, computes layout2d, then the changed code reads visible WCO geometry and adjusts the position before writing CSS coordinates. All of this completes before the context view is positioned and usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous browser Window Controls Overlay geometry lookup via navigator.windowControlsOverlay.getTitlebarAreaRect()
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per ContextView layout; one active shared context view for the service path, or once per independently visible hover layout. Existing per-frame action-widget animation yields one lookup per frame, not per action/item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scenario already synchronously wrote temporary position styles and measured page position and total view size, but did not query WCO geometry or run the fixed-size overlap adjustment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The lookup is on the positioning critical path, after existing DOM measurement and before style writes. Repository usage treats the same API as a direct geometry getter; there is no evidence it performs IPC, forces an additional DOM layout, or has input-dependent cost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup and constant-size adjustment per visible ContextView layout. Most relayouts occur once on show or on container/hover content changes; an existing action-widget animation can invoke layout once per animation frame, but there is still only one active service context view and no multiplication by menu items or document size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous on the UI thread; calls are serialized by the event loop. Existing layout events and animation frames are not given new parallelism or queues by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The code intentionally does not cache WCO geometry, so both cold and warm layouts perform one lookup when the overlay is visible. Unsupported or invisible overlays return before allocating the helper's validation and strip arrays. There is no positive/negative cache or coalescing behavior changed by the PR.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed call path, synchronous placement, and fixed cardinality; low evidence that the browser getter or constant-size allocations are expensive enough to cause user-visible latency or frame loss.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The implementation cost of Chromium's WCO geometry getter is not established in repository evidence, but the changed cardinality is strictly one per layout and the helper processes only two strips. This is insufficient to establish a meaningful regression even on the existing short per-frame animation path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added work is bounded and small relative to the pre-existing forced DOM measurements in the same layout pass, with no collection scaling, fan-out, concurrency burst, or retained lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a first-level or nested submenu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Submenu creation constructs and measures the menu, computes its viewport placement, then the changed code reads WCO geometry and adjusts the result before setting left/top. The submenu cannot be displayed at its final position until this synchronous work completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous browser Window Controls Overlay geometry lookup
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per newly opened submenu level, independent of submenu child count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening each submenu already performed synchronous style and DOM geometry reads and menu construction; it did not read WCO geometry or apply the fixed-size two-strip adjustment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the submenu-open critical path after pre-existing getComputedStyle and two getBoundingClientRect measurements. No evidence shows a new layout flush or cross-process operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one WCO lookup and one constant-size overlap calculation for each submenu level when that level is opened. Cost scales with user-opened nesting depth, not with the number of submenu actions; menu construction and DOM measurement already scale with action count before this change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Submenus open serially in response to keyboard/pointer interaction. No Promise fan-out, background task, limiter, or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used. Unsupported or invisible overlays take an immediate return; visible overlays are read once for each newly opened submenu so current geometry is used. Re-focusing an already-created submenu does not rerun _layoutSubmenu in the shown path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the new work occurs once per opened level and is synchronous; no evidence supports a material latency, CPU, GC, rendering, or IPC regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native getter latency is not measured, but realistic depth is small and the changed work does not scale with the 200-item tall-menu case beyond the existing menu construction/measurement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The change adds constant bounded work to an already geometry-heavy, user-triggered open path and does not add per-item work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compute title-bar geometry for existing titlebar layout callers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing titlebar minimum-height getters continue using getWCOTitlebarAreaRect directly. The new exported helper is not invoked by those callers, so their startup/layout critical path is unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: No changed multiplicity for titlebar parts; the helper addition itself performs no eager work at module load.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged synchronous getter execution in existing titlebar layout.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing titlebar callers remain uncached and unchanged. The new helper has no module-level state and cannot retain geometry or objects.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence based on complete symbol search and the pure new module.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: repository call-site search confirms only the two new UI placement call sites use getVisibleWCOTitlebarAreaRect.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change on existing titlebar layout or startup paths; importing the helper module adds only declarations with no eager runtime initialization.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 7 changed files and traced context-view show/relayout, per-frame action-widget relayout, hover resize, submenu opening, and existing titlebar geometry use. The PR adds one synchronous WCO getter plus fixed two-strip arithmetic per affected layout/open. It introduces no scaling boundary calls, cache growth, retained resources, unbounded concurrency, or additional DOM layout flush proven by the code, so no performance finding was submitted.
